issue_write_not_visible.title: Task is outside this actor's visibility
issue_write_not_visible.description: Issue writes are open by default, but only for tasks the actor can already read. {{issue}} is not visible to {{actor}}, so its comment, update, child, and assignment channels are all closed — the wall is visibility, not the write itself.
issue_write_not_visible.whoCanAct: {{assignee}}, and any agent or board member the task is visible to.
issue_write_not_visible.sanctionedPath: Ask the board to widen visibility for {{actor}}, or create a child issue with the request in its description (issue creation is a separate, open write path) and let its assignee act.

issue_write_actor_class_excluded.title: This actor class cannot write to tasks
issue_write_actor_class_excluded.description: Default-open issue writes are a standard-trust privilege. Low-trust, skill-test, and task-bridge scopes keep their existing tight walls, so {{actor}} cannot write to {{issue}} no matter who it acts for.
issue_write_actor_class_excluded.whoCanAct: A standard-trust agent in this company, or a board member.
issue_write_actor_class_excluded.sanctionedPath: Report the request upward and let a standard-trust agent make the write — actor-class scope cannot be widened per task.

issue_write_responsible_user_ceiling.title: Responsible user not authorized
issue_write_responsible_user_ceiling.description: This action was denied because {{responsible}} — the user this run acts on behalf of — does not have permission to perform it. The agent may be allowed, but a run can never exceed the permissions of the user it acts for, so the action is blocked. The write to {{issue}} was refused for that reason.
issue_write_responsible_user_ceiling.whoCanAct: {{responsible}} once authorized, or anyone already permitted to write to {{issue}}.
issue_write_responsible_user_ceiling.sanctionedPath: Grant {{responsible}} the required permission, or have someone who is authorized take this action instead.

issue_write_responsible_user_unavailable.title: Responsible user unavailable
issue_write_responsible_user_unavailable.description: This run acts on behalf of {{responsible}}, but that account was removed or deactivated, so its permissions can no longer be evaluated. The agent's own permissions are not enough on their own — every action still requires an active responsible user. The write to {{issue}} was refused for that reason.
issue_write_responsible_user_unavailable.whoCanAct: A board member, or {{actor}} once it has an active responsible user.
issue_write_responsible_user_unavailable.sanctionedPath: Mark the work blocked and reassign a responsible user (or reactivate the account) before the agent continues.

issue_write_assignee_run_lock.title: Another agent's run owns this task
issue_write_assignee_run_lock.description: {{assignee}} has {{issue}} checked out and a run is live. Checkout and run ownership stay assignee-scoped even though writes are open, so field edits belong to the run that holds the lock until it finishes.
issue_write_assignee_run_lock.whoCanAct: {{assignee}}'s live run, or an agent holding the manage-active-checkouts permission.
issue_write_assignee_run_lock.sanctionedPath: Comment instead of patching — comments stay open and wake {{assignee}} — or wait for the run to release the lock and retry.

cross_issue_influence_cap_exceeded.title: This run has spent its cross-issue write budget
cross_issue_influence_cap_exceeded.description: A single heartbeat run may make at most {{cap}} cross-issue comments or task updates combined{{attemptDetail}}. The cap bounds runaway comment sprays and loops — it is a rate backstop, not a permission decision, so {{actor}} is still allowed to write to {{issue}}.
cross_issue_influence_cap_exceeded.whoCanAct: {{actor}} on its next heartbeat run, or {{assignee}} on {{issue}} directly.
cross_issue_influence_cap_exceeded.sanctionedPath: Consolidate what is left into one comment on your own task, or end the run and continue on the next heartbeat — the budget resets per run.

cross_issue_influence_run_context_requir.title: Cross-issue writes need a run to attribute them to
cross_issue_influence_run_context_requir.description: Every agent comment and task update is attributed to a heartbeat run so the cross-issue cap can be counted and the audit trail can name who acted for whom. This request arrived without a valid run, so it could not be contained.
cross_issue_influence_run_context_requir.whoCanAct: {{actor}}, once the request carries its own run id.
cross_issue_influence_run_context_requir.sanctionedPath: Send the `X-Paperclip-Run-Id` header with your current run (`$PAPERCLIP_RUN_ID`) and retry.

issue_write_attribution_spoof_rejected.title: Responsible user cannot be chosen by the caller
issue_write_attribution_spoof_rejected.description: `onBehalfOfUserId` is derived from the authenticated actor, never from the request body — an agent cannot pick the human whose authority it rides. The attempt was recorded in the audit log.
issue_write_attribution_spoof_rejected.whoCanAct: {{actor}} itself: the write is allowed, only the chosen attribution is not.
issue_write_attribution_spoof_rejected.sanctionedPath: Remove `onBehalfOfUserId` from the request and retry; the server fills in {{responsible}} from your run.

lifecycle.spekoReconnect: Reverify this voice persona and update its signed session tools. Existing task assignments stay attached to their history.

lifecycle.agentmailRemove: Disconnect email and retain task history.
lifecycle.slackReconnect: Reconnect verifies or replaces credentials for this same Slack app. It does not reinstall the app or change its workspace or channel membership.
lifecycle.slackRemove: Paperclip archives the endpoint, stops new ingress, and retires its saved Slack credentials. It does not uninstall the Slack app: the app remains installed, and its bot remains in channels, until you remove them in Slack.
lifecycle.githubReconnect: Reconnect verifies this same App and installation, then updates its webhook URL, secret, and secure delivery settings. It does not reinstall the App or change repository access.
lifecycle.githubRemove: Paperclip archives the endpoint, stops new ingress, and retires its saved App key and webhook secret. It does not uninstall the GitHub App: the App, its installations, and its webhook settings remain until you remove or update them on GitHub.
lifecycle.discordReconnect: Reconnect verifies this same Discord application and server installation. It does not add or remove the bot from the server.
lifecycle.discordRemove: Paperclip archives the endpoint, stops its Paperclip Gateway connection, and retires its saved bot token. It does not uninstall the bot: the bot remains in the Discord server, and the application remains in the Developer Portal, until you remove them there.
lifecycle.teamsReconnect: Reconnect verifies this same Microsoft app, tenant, and bot identity. It does not upload or reinstall the Teams app.
lifecycle.teamsRemove: Paperclip archives the endpoint, stops new ingress, and retires its saved client secret. It does not uninstall the Teams app: the Entra app registration, Azure Bot, custom Teams app, and Teams installations remain until you remove them in Microsoft.
lifecycle.photonReconnect: Reconnect verifies the same Photon project and line allocation, then recovers eligible missed messages.
lifecycle.photonRemove: Disconnect archives this channel and removes its saved secret. Your Photon project, number, subscription, and Messages history remain in Photon.
lifecycle.telegramReconnect: Reconnect verifies this same BotFather bot and automatically refreshes its Paperclip webhook and command menu.
lifecycle.telegramRemove: Paperclip archives the endpoint and queues durable removal of its Telegram webhook and command menu. After Telegram confirms that cleanup, Paperclip retires the saved token. The BotFather bot and its chat memberships remain until you remove them in Telegram.

chatSetup.teamsIntro: Use your own Microsoft app credentials for this bot.
chatSetup.teamsRequirements: This setup requires a Microsoft 365 work or school organization where you can register an Entra app, create an Azure Bot, and upload or install a Teams app. Personal or free Teams accounts at teams.live.com cannot complete this setup. This release supports Microsoft 365 commercial cloud tenants only; GCC, GCC High, DoD, and Microsoft 365 operated by 21Vianet are not supported yet.
chatSetup.teamsStep1: In Microsoft Entra, create a single-tenant app registration. Copy its Application (client) ID and Directory (tenant) ID, then create a client secret and copy its value.
chatSetup.teamsStep2: In Azure, create an Azure Bot. Choose Single Tenant, use that Application ID, set its messaging endpoint to the Paperclip URL below, and add the Microsoft Teams channel.
chatSetup.teamsStep3: In Teams Developer Portal, create an app, add a bot with the same Application ID, then apply the manifest settings shown below. The block binds the Teams resource-specific consent permissions to that Entra app; these are not Microsoft Graph permissions in Entra. These permissions let the installed app receive every message in a team or group chat without an @mention, so describe that access to installers. Download the package and install it in the target team or group chat.
chatSetup.portalFieldMapDescription: Use these exact portal sections and reuse the same Application ID in all three places.
chatSetup.portalStep1: Microsoft Entra admin center · App registrations: select New registration, choose Accounts in this organizational directory only (Single tenant), then select Register. Copy Application (client) ID and Directory (tenant) ID. Under Certificates & secrets · Client secrets, select New client secret and copy its Value, not its Secret ID.
chatSetup.portalStep2: Azure · Create Azure Bot: set Microsoft App ID to Single Tenant, set Creation type to Use existing app registration, and enter the Application ID and Tenant ID above. After creation, open Settings · Configuration and paste the Paperclip Messaging endpoint; then open Settings · Channels and enable Microsoft Teams.
chatSetup.portalStep3: Teams Developer Portal · Apps: select New app. Under Configure · App features · Bot, add an existing bot using the same Application ID; enable Personal, Team, and Group chat scopes plus file support. Under Configure · Permissions, add the two RSC Application permissions shown below. Complete the required app details and icons, explain that the app can receive every message in an installed team or group chat, then download the app package.
chatSetup.portalStep4: Microsoft Teams · Apps · Manage your apps: select Upload an app · Upload a custom app, choose the downloaded package, and install it in each intended personal chat, group chat, or team. If upload is unavailable, a Teams administrator must enable or approve custom apps.
chatSetup.manifestCopyNote: Enter the Application / Client ID above before copying so the block contains the real bot identity. chatSetup.teamsSsoNote: Paperclip does not use Teams single sign-on in this release. The copied webApplicationInfo entry only associates the RSC permissions with the same Entra Application ID. chatSetup.teamsRscNote: The two application RSC permissions let the bot receive every message, without an @mention, in each team or group chat where it is installed. Paperclip retains and acts only on messages admitted by your Paperclip reach and access rules. Make this provider access clear in the app description shown to installers.
chatSetup.teamsFileNote: This release supports personal chats, group chats, and standard team channels—not private channels. supportsFiles: true enables native file receipt and consent-based sending in personal chats; channel and group-chat files need a separate Microsoft Graph connection and are not ingested here.

interactionGovernance.heading: Interaction governance
interactionGovernance.description: Thread interactions are open by default: Anyone in the organization — the board or any agent, including the one that asked — can respond. Narrow a kind only when you need to. Default policy is the audience new cards get when the requester does not ask for one; Cap narrows every request of that kind and can never widen one. Tool-approval confirmations always stay Human only.

effects.defaultAnyone: New cards are open — the board or any agent can respond, including the one that asked.
effects.defaultNotCreator: New cards exclude the agent that created them, so the answer comes from someone else.
effects.defaultHumanOnly: New cards wait for a person on the board. Agents are turned away.
effects.capAnyone: A request keeps whatever audience it asks for.
effects.capNotCreator: Even a card that asks for Anyone is narrowed to exclude its creator.
effects.capHumanOnly: Every card of this kind waits for a person, whatever it asked for.

instanceExperimental.description: Opt into features that are still being evaluated before they become default behavior.
instanceExperimental.warningTitle: Experimental features may break at any time.
instanceExperimental.warningDescription: These features are opt-in and come with no compatibility guarantees. They may change, break, or be removed without notice. Avoid relying on them for critical or production workflows.
instanceExperimental.featuresDescription: Optional product features that are still being evaluated.

agentChat.title: Agent Chat
agentChat.description: Talk to each agent in one ongoing conversation. Clarify goals and create tasks for execution. Chat leads the Work group and opens an agent rail beside the nav, and each chat's side panel shows the agent's tasks and artifacts as cards.
agentChat.footnote: Turning this off preserves conversations and lets active runs finish, but prevents new messages.

assistantConnections.title: Assistant connections (MCP)
assistantConnections.description: Connect Codex, Claude, and other assistants to your Paperclip organization. People sign in, select an organization once, and approve access to review work, delegate tasks, and add feedback.
assistantConnections.footnote: Requires an authenticated instance with a configured public URL. Takes effect immediately. Turning this off blocks assistant calls and event delivery; work already delegated continues.

betaSkills.title: Beta skills
betaSkills.description: Allow agents to pin beta releases of the Paperclip core skill. Disabling this returns every agent to the default live skill without removing saved pins.

builtInAgents.title: Built-in Agents
builtInAgents.description: Show Paperclip-managed built-in agent surfaces, including built-in roster badges, the Built-in agents tab, and built-in agent setup controls.

cases.title: Cases
cases.description: Durable work products (blog posts, tweet storms…) that tasks create and iterate on. Adds the Cases tab and the agent case API.
cases.footnote: Turning Cases off hides the tab and blocks the case API; existing case data is kept.

chatConnectors.title: Chat connectors
chatConnectors.description: Connect agents to Slack, Discord, Microsoft Teams, and Telegram conversations.
chatConnectors.footnote: Turning this off hides experimental chat setup and connected-task controls. Existing chat connections keep running. AgentMail, GitHub review bots, and tool connectors are controlled separately.

combinedInbox.title: Combined Inbox + Task List
combinedInbox.description: Fold Inbox into Tasks. One Tasks row carries the unread badge, and a Views menu reaches every inbox view (Mine, Unread, Blocked, Recent, Everything) and every task view.
combinedInbox.footnote: Old Inbox links redirect to the matching view. Turning this off restores the separate Inbox; no data changes.
combinedInbox.aria: Toggle combined inbox and task list experimental setting

conferenceRoom.title: Conference Room Chat
conferenceRoom.description: Adds a Conference Room — one chat where you and your whole team work together — plus the live activity feed and the redesigned onboarding. Also restyles task threads as chat bubbles. Turn off anytime to restore the classic UI.
conferenceRoom.aria: Toggle conference room chat experimental setting

decisions.title: Decisions
decisions.description: Show the Decisions item in the main sidebar — the attention home that surfaces the tasks awaiting your input — while the surface is still being evaluated.

environments.title: Enable Environments
environments.description: Show environment management in company settings and allow project and agent environment assignment controls.

externalObjects.title: Enable External Objects
externalObjects.description: Detect external URLs in issues and show resolved status for pull requests, tickets, and other referenced work objects.

isolatedWorkspaces.title: Enable Isolated Workspaces
isolatedWorkspaces.description: Show execution workspace controls in project configuration and allow isolated workspace behavior for new and existing task runs.

fastResponses.title: Experimental fast responses
fastResponses.description: Show Connections in company settings and allow short acknowledgements while agents begin work.

experimentalFileViewer.title: Experimental File Viewer
experimentalFileViewer.description: Show task detail controls for browsing and previewing workspace files relative to a task.

firstTaskPlanProposal.title: First task: propose with a plan document
firstTaskPlanProposal.description: When the user's first request is a single task, the chief of staff writes a short plan document and a checkbox card instead of a one-card confirmation. Applies to organizations created after the toggle is flipped.
firstTaskPlanProposal.aria: Toggle first task plan proposal experimental setting

githubReviewBots.title: GitHub review bots
githubReviewBots.description: Connect agents to GitHub with their own App identity to review pull requests and respond to issues.
githubReviewBots.footnote: Independent of Chat connectors. Turning this off hides setup and management; existing bots keep running. GitHub tool connections stay available.
githubReviewBots.aria: Toggle GitHub review bots experimental setting

grokBot.title: Grok Bot
grokBot.description: Connect an existing Grok Bot as an agent. Verify routine delivery and an authenticated reply before assigning work.
grokBot.footnote: Requires Assistant connections (MCP), Paperclip Runner, and authenticated public HTTPS. Usage is not reported. Turning this off blocks Grok calls and new dispatch.

memoryConnectors.title: Memory connectors
memoryConnectors.description: Connect Mem0, Zep, Supermemory, Cognee, and Honcho for long-term memory and context.
memoryConnectors.footnote: Turning this off hides setup for these connectors. Existing connections keep running.

muse.title: Muse — Personal agent
muse.description: Connect your personal Meta Muse. Pair it, detect its receiver, and verify an independent background reply before assigning tasks.
muse.footnote: Requires Paperclip Runner and an authenticated instance with a public HTTPS URL. Turning this off blocks new work; cleanup and stop evidence remain available. Provider usage and cost are unavailable.

openAiDot.title: OpenAI Dot
openAiDot.description: Add OpenAI Dot as a standalone agent choice. Pair your Dot and verify event delivery before assigning work.
openAiDot.footnote: Requires Assistant connections (MCP) and an authenticated instance with a public HTTPS URL. Turning this off blocks Dot calls and new work; saved connections are kept.

paperclipRunner.title: Paperclip Runner
paperclipRunner.description: Allow new Codex agents to select the experimental Rust Paperclip Runner, including authenticated runner ingress when a sandbox requires it. Onboarding continues to use legacy adapters. Turning this off hides the choice without affecting existing native runs.

simplifiedEnglishInteractions.title: Simplified English Interactions
simplifiedEnglishInteractions.description: Instruct agents to write user interactions (plan confirmations, questions, suggested tasks, checkbox prompts) in ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English, with brief context on what information the decision needs and what happens for each choice.
simplifiedEnglishInteractions.aria: Toggle simplified english interactions experimental setting

statusCards.title: Status Cards
statusCards.description: Enable the experimental shared status-card board and its gated API. Existing card data is kept when this is disabled.
statusCards.footnote: Enabling Status Cards also enables Summaries.

streamlinedUi.title: Streamlined UI
streamlinedUi.description: Use the simplified main sidebar, shared Tasks and Inbox presentation, focused task detail layout, and contextual navigation across Agents, Routines, Skills, and Settings.
streamlinedUi.footnote: Turning this off restores the legacy shell and navigation. Task and page data are unchanged.

summaries.title: Summaries
summaries.description: Show Summarizer-generated status slots on project and workspace pages, with on-demand refresh and revision history. Existing summary data is kept when this is disabled.
summaries.footnote: Status Cards requires Summaries. Disabling Summaries also disables Status Cards.

isolatedWorkspacesByDefault.title: Use Isolated Workspaces By Default
isolatedWorkspacesByDefault.description: Treat a project that has no execution workspace policy of its own as if it selected isolated workspaces, so its tasks get a per-task worktree instead of sharing the project checkout. A project that carries its own policy keeps it.
isolatedWorkspacesByDefault.aria: Toggle isolated workspaces by default experimental setting

developer.heading: Paperclip Developer Mode
developer.description: Internal tools for developing, testing, and debugging Paperclip.

autoRestart.title: Auto-Restart Dev Server When Idle
autoRestart.description: In `pnpm dev:once`, wait for all queued and running local agent runs to finish, then restart the server automatically when backend changes or migrations make the current boot stale.

managedEnvironmentOnly.title: Managed Environment Only
managedEnvironmentOnly.description: Hide the local environment and run all agents in the platform-managed environment.
managedEnvironmentOnly.aria: Toggle managed environment only experimental setting

paperclipDeveloperMode.title: Paperclip Developer Mode
paperclipDeveloperMode.description: Show internal Paperclip maintainer tools and observability links, including Honeycomb trace queries on run pages.
paperclipDeveloperMode.aria: Toggle Paperclip developer mode experimental setting

worktree.title: Run tasks in this worktree
worktree.description: This is an isolated git-worktree preview instance. Turn this on to let the scheduler execute runs here. Only tasks created after enabling will run automatically — copied/pre-existing tasks stay parked. Toggling off and on resets the cutoff.
worktree.instanceMismatch: This setting was armed in a different instance and copied here, so no tasks run automatically.
worktree.missingCutoff: This setting is missing its activation cutoff, so no tasks run automatically.
worktree.rearm: Toggle it off and back on to arm execution for tasks created here.

serverInfoDebugView.title: Server Info Debug View
serverInfoDebugView.description: Show a "Server" section in the account drawer with the current server restart time and running commit.
serverInfoDebugView.aria: Toggle server info debug view experimental setting

smokeLab.title: Smoke Lab
smokeLab.description: Add a "Smoke Lab" tab under Apps → Developer and an "Integration smoke" card on the dashboard for exercising every integration path against deterministic local fixtures (fake OAuth provider + loopback MCP servers). Private (non-public) deployments only.

taskPlanDecomposition.title: Task Plan Decomposition
taskPlanDecomposition.description: Show accepted-plan decomposition history on task detail pages. Intended for debugging and validating subtask creation behavior while the presentation is still being refined.
taskPlanDecomposition.aria: Toggle task plan decomposition panel experimental setting

legacy.heading: Legacy
legacy.description: These features are going to be removed.

classicTaskInterface.title: Classic Task Interface
classicTaskInterface.description: Restores the previous task detail page: the page-level header with inline description editing, the plain comment thread, and the fixed Properties sidebar. Chat-only features — streaming activity folding, inline plan and question cards, the three-mode composer — are unavailable in the classic view.
classicTaskInterface.footnote: Switching takes effect immediately. No task data is affected.
classicTaskInterface.aria: Toggle classic task interface experimental setting

goalsSidebarLink.title: Goals Sidebar Link
goalsSidebarLink.description: Restore the Goals item in the main sidebar while the goals surface is being evaluated.
goalsSidebarLink.aria: Toggle goals sidebar link experimental setting

concurrency.coalesceDescription: Keep one follow-up run queued while an active run is still working.
concurrency.alwaysDescription: Queue every trigger occurrence, even if several runs stack up.
concurrency.skipDescription: Drop overlapping trigger occurrences while the routine is already active.

catchUp.skipDescription: Ignore schedule windows that were missed while paused.
catchUp.enqueueDescription: Catch up missed schedule windows after recovery; sub-hourly schedules are combined into one catch-up run, slower schedules replay each missed window up to a cap.

activityGate.alwaysDescription: Fire on the schedule no matter what — the default behavior.
activityGate.requireTitle: Skip when there's been no activity since the last run
activityGate.requireDescription: On a scheduled tick, only run if something happened since the last run that finished. Lets a watcher-style routine stay asleep while the system is settled instead of burning tokens.

signingModeDescriptions.bearer: Send Authorization: Bearer <secret> with each request.

signingModeDescriptions.none: No authentication — the webhook URL itself acts as a shared secret.

pathInstructions.title: How to get a full path

steps.step1: Open Finder and navigate to the folder.
steps.step3: Hold the Option (⌥) key — "Copy" changes to "Copy as Pathname".
steps.step4: Click "Copy as Pathname", then paste here.

mac.tip: You can also open Terminal, type cd, drag the folder into the terminal window, and press Enter. Then type pwd to see the full path.

steps.step1: Open File Explorer and navigate to the folder.
steps.step2: Click in the address bar at the top — the full path will appear.
steps.step3: Copy the path, then paste here.

windows.tip: Alternatively, hold Shift and right-click the folder, then select "Copy as path".

steps.step1: Open a terminal and navigate to the directory with cd.
steps.step2: Run pwd to print the full path.
steps.step3: Copy the output and paste here.

linux.tip: In most file managers, Ctrl+L reveals the full path in the address bar.
